players.pls: Founded by CMU adversarial-ML researchers, Gray Swan runs the field's largest crowdsourced red-teaming arenas — 15,000+ researchers and millions of recorded attack attempts — alongside Shade automated red-teaming and Cygnal runtime defense. Its challenges have informed pre-release safety evaluations for frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind, plus work with the US AI Security Institute.

players.name: Pillar Security
players.tagline: Unified lifecycle security for AI agents
players.pls: Israeli-founded startup unifying AI discovery, posture management, red-teaming, and runtime guardrails for what it calls the agentic workforce, and co-author of the SAIL framework for secure AI development. Named a 2026 Gartner Cool Vendor in AI Software Security and a representative vendor in Gartner's 2026 Guardian Agents market guide — a rising independent amid consolidation.

categories.name: Voice AI
categories.pls: The layer that lets software listen and talk: speech-to-text, lifelike text-to-speech, and orchestration platforms that wire both around LLMs into agents that handle real phone calls. It matters because voice is becoming a default interface for support, scheduling, sales, and AI companions. The mid-2026 dynamic is consolidation up the stack: ElevenLabs (valued at $11B in February 2026) now sells a full agent platform, speech-to-speech models like OpenAI's gpt-realtime are collapsing the old three-model pipeline, big tech is buying in (Meta acquired PlayAI in 2025), and orchestration players race to be the default runtime.

players.name: ElevenLabs
players.pls: The best-known AI voice company, founded by Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski. It began with ultra-realistic text-to-speech and voice cloning and now sells dubbing, music, and a full voice-agent platform. Raised a $500M Series D at an $11B valuation in February 2026, led by Sequoia, as it eyes an eventual IPO.

players.name: OpenAI Realtime API
players.pls: OpenAI's API for building talking agents with a single speech-to-speech model instead of a separate STT-LLM-TTS chain, cutting latency and preserving tone and emotion. The gpt-realtime model and Realtime API went GA in August 2025 with SIP phone-calling support, and they now underpin many production customer-service and consumer voice applications.

players.name: Deepgram
players.pls: San Francisco speech-AI company whose fast, inexpensive Nova-3 transcription API is a workhorse behind many voice products. In late 2025 it launched Flux, a conversational speech-recognition model that natively handles turn-taking for agents (multilingual support followed in 2026), and it bundles STT, Aura TTS, and a Voice Agent API for enterprises.

players.name: AssemblyAI
players.pls: Developer-focused speech AI company offering accurate transcription plus understanding features like summarization, sentiment, and PII redaction. Its Universal-Streaming model, launched in 2025, delivers roughly 300 ms streaming transcripts designed for voice agents, and the company publishes widely cited voice-AI industry research. A default alternative to Deepgram for transcription APIs.

players.name: Cartesia
players.pls: San Francisco lab founded by Stanford state-space-model researchers, building voice AI for real-time use. Its Sonic-3 text-to-speech renders speech in under 100 ms, fast enough for natural phone conversation, and became available on AWS SageMaker JumpStart in February 2026. Raised a $64M Series B in 2025 and now sells Line, an end-to-end voice-agent stack.

players.name: Vapi
players.tagline: Developer platform for phone voice agents
players.pls: API-first orchestration platform that lets developers assemble phone and web voice agents from any mix of speech-to-text, LLM, and TTS providers, with tool calling and telephony built in. It is one of the default choices for voice-agent builders; 2026 industry comparisons report over 300M calls and 2.5M assistants created on the platform.

players.name: Retell AI
players.tagline: Production voice agents for call operations
players.pls: Y Combinator-backed platform for building and operating AI phone agents, popular for appointment booking, lead qualification, and support at scale. It differentiates on operations: batch calling, A/B testing, analytics, and SOC 2/HIPAA compliance, with round-trip latency around 300-500 ms in 2026 platform comparisons. A frequent head-to-head rival of Vapi.

players.name: LiveKit
players.pls: Open-source WebRTC infrastructure and Agents framework that moves audio between users and models with millisecond latency; it famously carries voice traffic for ChatGPT's voice mode. Raised a $45M Series B in April 2025, and its 2026 Agents releases added smarter interruption handling, cementing it as default plumbing for serious voice applications.

players.name: Pipecat (Daily)
players.pls: MIT-licensed Python framework from video-infrastructure company Daily for orchestrating real-time voice and multimodal agents with pluggable STT, LLM, and TTS pipelines. It reached v1.0 in April 2026 and is the main open-source alternative to hosted agent platforms; Daily monetizes through Pipecat Cloud managed hosting for production deployments.

players.name: Hume AI
players.pls: New York research company focused on emotion in voice. Its Empathic Voice Interface speaks and listens with measured emotional expression; EVI 3, released in May 2025, added on-the-fly voice design and was preferred over GPT-4o's voice in the company's blind tests. Its Octave TTS and APIs serve health, coaching, and companion apps.

players.name: Rime
players.pls: San Francisco voice startup specializing in fast, demographically diverse synthetic voices for business phone calls - drive-thrus and contact centers rather than audiobooks. Its Arcana spoken-language model, launched in 2025, produces convincingly imperfect conversational speech with laughs and hesitations, and on-premise deployment options appeal to telecom, food-service, and healthcare buyers.

players.name: Sesame
players.tagline: Viral voice companions and AI glasses
players.pls: Startup from Oculus co-founder Brendan Iribe whose eerily natural 'Maya' conversational voice demo went viral in early 2025 and reset expectations for humanlike speech. It raised a $250M Series B in October 2025 and opened its companion-app beta, with lightweight AI glasses as the long-term bet; it also open-sourced its CSM-1B speech model.

players.name: Speechify
players.pls: Speechify is a consumer text-to-speech app that reads documents, articles, and books aloud in natural and celebrity voices across web, mobile, and browser extensions. Popular with students and people with dyslexia or ADHD, it has broad name recognition beyond developer circles and also offers an API and AI voiceover and dubbing tools.

categories.name: Media Generation
categories.pls: Models and products that turn text and reference media into images and video, plus avatar tools that put a photorealistic presenter on camera. This layer is collapsing the cost of ads, product imagery, film previsualization, and corporate video. The mid-2026 dynamic: Google (Veo 3.1, Nano Banana) and Chinese labs (Kuaishou's Kling 3.0, ByteDance's Seedream, MiniMax's Hailuo) set the pace on quality and price; OpenAI shut down its viral Sora app in April 2026; open-weight FLUX anchors the builder ecosystem; and avatar platforms like HeyGen, at $200M ARR, prove the enterprise business model.

players.name: Google Veo
players.pls: Google DeepMind's video model family generates cinematic clips with synchronized dialogue, music, and sound effects in a single pass. Veo 3.1 shipped in October 2025 and reaches consumers through the Gemini app and the Flow filmmaking tool; paired with the viral 'Nano Banana' Gemini image models, it made Google the platform to beat by mid-2026.

players.name: OpenAI (Sora & GPT Image)
players.pls: OpenAI's media generation spans the gpt-image models behind ChatGPT's hugely popular image creation and Sora 2, whose TikTok-style app topped the App Store after launching in September 2025. In a striking reversal, OpenAI discontinued the Sora app on April 26, 2026, with the API ending that September, refocusing video inside ChatGPT and on enterprise products.

players.name: Midjourney
players.pls: Independent, self-funded San Francisco lab whose Discord-born image generator remains the aesthetic benchmark for stylized art. It added a first video model, V1, in June 2025, licensed its aesthetic technology to Meta that August, and began rolling out its V8 image model in alpha in early 2026 with a rebuilt dataset and stronger personalization.

players.name: Black Forest Labs
players.pls: German lab founded by the original Stable Diffusion researchers; its FLUX models are the open-weight standard for image generation, embedded across creative tools and API platforms. It released FLUX.2 in November 2025, including open-weight variants, and closed roughly $300M at a $3.25B valuation, making it Europe's leading image-AI company.

players.name: Runway
players.tagline: AI video for filmmakers and studios
players.pls: New York pioneer of AI video for professional creatives, with fine-grained editing controls, Act-Two performance capture, and studio partnerships including Lionsgate and AMC. Its Gen-4.5 model, released in late 2025, topped video-generation leaderboards, and the company raised a $308M Series D in April 2025 at around a $3B valuation while pushing toward general world models.

players.name: Kling AI (Kuaishou)
players.pls: Video generator from Chinese short-video giant Kuaishou, widely rated among the world's best for realism and character consistency at aggressive prices. Kling 3.0, launched February 5, 2026, produces multi-shot 15-second scenes with native multilingual audio; Kuaishou says Kling has served over 60M creators and generated 600M+ videos since June 2024.

players.name: Luma AI
players.tagline: Frontier video lab with Saudi backing
players.pls: Bay Area lab behind the Dream Machine platform and Ray model line; Ray3, launched in September 2025, was pitched as the first reasoning video model with studio-grade HDR output. It raised a $900M Series C led by Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN in November 2025 to build a 2-gigawatt supercluster and train frontier multimodal world models.

players.name: Hailuo (MiniMax)
players.pls: Video product from Shanghai AI company MiniMax, praised for realistic physics and strong instruction-following since Hailuo 02's viral 2025 demos, and a favorite of creators on price-for-quality. Parent MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in early 2026 in a roughly $540M IPO, among the first Chinese LLM startups to go public.

players.name: ByteDance Seedream & Seedance
players.pls: ByteDance's Seed lab builds Seedream (image) and Seedance (video), distributed through CapCut, Doubao, and Dreamina. Seedance 1.0 topped Artificial Analysis text-to-video rankings at its June 2025 launch, and Seedream 4.0 led image-editing leaderboards that September, turning ByteDance into a top-tier media-model lab almost overnight.

players.name: HeyGen
players.pls: Los Angeles-based leader in AI avatar video: type a script and a photorealistic presenter delivers it in over 175 languages, with lip-synced video translation and interactive avatar agents. HeyGen doubled to $200M ARR by June 2026, reportedly without burning cash, as marketing, sales, and training teams replaced studio shoots.

players.name: Synthesia
players.pls: London company that pioneered corporate avatar video, used by a majority of the Fortune 100 for training and internal communications. It passed $100M ARR in early 2025 after a $180M Series D valued it at $2.1B, and its Express-2 avatars added full-body gestures and more natural delivery. The enterprise counterpart to HeyGen.

players.name: Ideogram
players.pls: Toronto startup founded by ex-Google Imagen researchers, best known for rendering legible typography - logos, posters, memes - where rivals garble letters. Ideogram 3.0, released in March 2025, improved realism and added style references, and its Canvas tool targets designers. A free tier and API keep it a favorite for graphic-design workflows.

players.name: Adobe Firefly
players.pls: Adobe Firefly is Adobe's family of generative image, video, and design models, trained for commercial safety and built directly into Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, and Express. In 2026 it added agentic 'Creative Agent' features and support for partner models, making it the generative layer most working designers and marketers actually touch day to day.

players.name: Stability AI
players.pls: Stability AI popularized open-weight image generation with Stable Diffusion, whose releasable models seeded much of the creative-AI ecosystem. It continues to ship open and commercial models across image, video, audio, and 3D, positioning itself as the open alternative to closed generators from OpenAI, Google, and Midjourney.

players.name: Pika
players.pls: Pika is a well-funded text- and image-to-video generator known for accessible, social-first creative effects that morph and transform footage. Aimed at everyday creators rather than studios, it competes with Runway, Luma, and Kling in the fast-moving short-form AI-video space.

categories.name: CLIs & Interfaces
categories.pls: Where you actually run AI: terminal-first tools — agent multiplexers and AI-native terminals — alongside the desktop apps and editors that have gone agent-first. The flagship coding CLIs live under Coding Agents and the model-agnostic runtimes under Model Harnesses; these are the terminals, launchers, editors, and desktops you drive them all from.

players.name: Warp
players.pls: Warp rebuilt the terminal around agents: multi-step Agent Mode in your shell, and since April 2026 universal support for running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode side by side with vertical tabs, status indicators, and code review. Credit-based pricing runs from a free tier to a $20 Build plan; Warp Drive shares context across a team.

players.name: Claude Desktop
players.pls: Claude's desktop app grew from a chat window into an agent workspace: Cowork grants folder access for multi-step file and document work, computer use drives real apps on screen, and MCP connectors plug in tools and data. As of July 2026 sessions can run remotely, continuing server-side and reachable from web or phone.

players.name: ChatGPT Desktop
players.tagline: Chat, Work, and Codex in one app
players.pls: OpenAI's July 2026 desktop app merges Chat, the new ChatGPT Work agent, and Codex on macOS and Windows. It works directly with local apps — editing open files in IDEs with reviewable diffs, pairing with terminals and docs — plus a companion window and voice mode for hands-on tasks alongside your other windows.

players.name: VS Code
players.pls: VS Code's 2026 releases turned Copilot agent mode into a first-class workflow: an Agents window in Stable, a standalone companion app for parallel sessions, MCP server bridging, terminal control, and agentic browser tools. Sessions sync to GitHub, and remote steering lets you leave agents working and check in from any device.

players.name: Zed
players.pls: Zed pairs the fastest editor in its class — Rust, GPU-rendered — with parallel agents, the open Zeta2 edit-prediction model, and hooks for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. It co-created the Agent Client Protocol with JetBrains in January 2026, now supported by 20+ agents and 10+ editors, and raised a $32M Sequoia-led Series B.

players.name: cmux
players.tagline: Native Mac terminal for agent fleets
players.pls: An open-source macOS terminal built on Ghostty for running coding agents in parallel: vertical tabs, smart notifications when an agent needs you, a built-in browser, and native panes for every subagent an orchestrator spawns. Any terminal agent works out of the box — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Aider, Goose — making cmux the iTerm2 of the agent era.

players.name: Aider
players.pls: Aider remains the benchmark for AI pair-programming in the terminal: it maps your repository, coordinates multi-file edits, and auto-commits each change with sensible messages, working with dozens of cloud and local models. Years after launch it is still the go-to for developers who want full open-source control of an agentic coding loop built around git.

players.name: JetBrains Junie
players.pls: Junie left beta in June 2026 as the coding agent across IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, and the rest of the JetBrains family. It plans before coding, debugs with the real IDE debugger, reviews PRs with project context, and topped the independent SWE-Rebench agent benchmark; the GA rebuild runs on the Agent Client Protocol it co-authored with Zed.

players.name: Raycast
players.tagline: The Mac launcher that became an AI hub
players.pls: Raycast folds AI into the fastest path on a Mac: a launcher opening in under 50ms that also chats, runs commands, and pipes GPT-5.5, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and any OpenAI-compatible model through 2,000+ extensions. Auto Model picks the right model per task; Pro with unlimited AI runs $8 a month.

players.name: herdr
players.pls: A single 10MB Rust binary that multiplexes AI coding agents the way tmux multiplexes shells: every agent gets a real PTY, and zero-config heuristics show who is idle, working, blocked, or done at a glance. A persistent server keeps agents alive when you detach — even over ssh. It hit #1 on GitHub Trending for Rust in June 2026 with 12k+ stars.

players.name: Jan
players.pls: Jan is a local-first desktop client that runs open-weight models — Llama, Gemma, Qwen, GPT-OSS — fully offline, with cloud models optional. An early Model Context Protocol adopter, it lets local models call tools, search, and files, and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on localhost for other apps to build against.

categories.name: Research Assistants & Literature
categories.pls: AI tools built for research itself — searching and synthesizing the scientific literature, extracting findings from papers, and generating and stress-testing hypotheses. These are field-agnostic assistants a historian, chemist, or genomics researcher would each use the same way, spanning free nonprofit tools and venture-backed products, plus the science-specific surfaces the major AI labs launched in 2026.

players.name: Elicit
players.pls: Elicit helps researchers run literature reviews with AI: it searches across more than a hundred million papers, extracts data into structured tables, and summarizes findings with citations. Used by millions of researchers and spun out of the nonprofit Ought, it is one of the most recognizable AI-for-research tools and a common recommendation in university library guides.

players.name: Consensus
players.pls: Consensus is an AI search engine over peer-reviewed literature that answers questions directly from findings across hundreds of millions of papers, with a 'Consensus Meter' summarizing how much studies agree. Aimed at researchers, clinicians, and students, it competes with Elicit and SciSpace as a go-to for evidence-grounded answers.

players.name: Semantic Scholar
players.pls: Semantic Scholar is the Allen Institute for AI's free academic search engine, indexing hundreds of millions of papers with AI-powered citation context and its ScholarQA assistant for literature synthesis. Nonprofit and partly open-source, it underpins many other research tools and is a default, no-cost starting point for scientists in every field.

players.name: SciSpace
players.pls: SciSpace is an AI research platform for finding, reading, and understanding papers, with an explain-as-you-read assistant, connections across hundreds of millions of documents, and reference-manager integrations. Its agent can chain external tools and databases, making it a broad workspace for literature review and academic writing.

players.name: scite
players.pls: scite analyzes how papers cite each other — whether a citation supports, contrasts, or merely mentions a claim — turning the citation graph into a signal of how well findings hold up. With millions of users and an MCP server that feeds its citation data to AI assistants, it helps researchers judge reliability, not just relevance.

players.name: FutureHouse
players.pls: FutureHouse is a nonprofit building AI agents for science, including PaperQA for high-accuracy literature synthesis and Robin, a multi-agent system that proposed a real drug-repurposing candidate. Backed by Eric Schmidt and paired with a commercial arm, it aims at automating parts of the discovery process, not just search.

players.name: Gemini Co-Scientist
players.pls: Google's AI co-scientist is a multi-agent research system built on Gemini that generates, debates, and ranks novel hypotheses and proposes experiments, part of a broader 'Gemini for Science' push alongside NotebookLM literature tools. It targets the ideation stage of research in biology and beyond.

players.name: OpenAI for Science (Prism)
players.pls: Prism is OpenAI's AI-native workspace for scientists, powered by its frontier GPT-5 models and open to researchers, part of a dedicated OpenAI for Science effort that also produced life-science-specific models. It positions general frontier models as research collaborators for hypothesis work, analysis, and writing across disciplines.

players.name: Undermind
players.pls: Undermind is an agentic search assistant that reads full papers rather than abstracts, running multi-step searches to surface hard-to-find research. Adopted by scientists at pharma companies and top universities, it targets the deep, exhaustive literature searches that general search engines miss.

categories.name: AI for Life Sciences
categories.pls: AI models and platforms built specifically for biology and drug discovery — predicting protein structures, designing new proteins and molecules, reading genomes, and running discovery workflows. This vertical layer is aimed at bench and computational biologists rather than general developers, and for a genomics or bioinformatics lab it is where the field's most recognizable AI tools live.

players.name: AlphaFold
players.pls: AlphaFold, from Google DeepMind, predicts 3D protein structures from sequence with remarkable accuracy — work that won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and reshaped structural biology. Its free server and open database serve millions of researchers, while DeepMind spinout Isomorphic Labs extends the approach toward AI-driven drug design with major pharma partnerships.

players.name: EvolutionaryScale (ESM3)
players.pls: EvolutionaryScale builds the ESM family of protein language models, including ESM3, trained on billions of sequences to predict structure and function and to generate novel proteins. Founded by researchers behind the original ESM work and now part of the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, it is a cornerstone of protein AI used widely across bioinformatics.

players.name: Boltz
players.pls: Boltz is an open-source, permissively licensed biomolecular model from MIT that predicts 3D structures and binding affinity, rivaling AlphaFold3-class systems. Adopted across pharma and academia and released freely, it is the natural open alternative for structure and drug-binding prediction, with commercial API layers now emerging around it.

players.name: Chai Discovery
players.pls: Chai Discovery builds frontier models for molecular structure prediction and de novo antibody and drug design, reporting wet-lab-validated hit rates and licensing deals with major pharma. Fast-growing and heavily funded, it is among the most visible startups applying foundation-model techniques directly to therapeutic discovery.

players.name: RFdiffusion (Baker Lab)
players.pls: RFdiffusion, from David Baker's Institute for Protein Design, uses diffusion models to design entirely new proteins — binders, enzymes, and therapeutics — foundational work tied to Baker's 2024 Nobel Prize. Open-sourced and widely used, it anchors the generative side of protein engineering and seeded startups like Xaira Therapeutics.

players.name: AlphaGenome
players.pls: AlphaGenome, from Google DeepMind, predicts how DNA sequence variants affect regulatory function across very long stretches of the genome, aimed at interpreting non-coding variation. Offered as a research API, it extends DeepMind's biology work from proteins into genomics — directly relevant to the questions a genomics lab asks.

players.name: Arc Institute (Evo 2)
players.pls: The Arc Institute builds open DNA foundation models — its Evo 2 model was trained on trillions of nucleotides with a very long context to predict and generate genomic sequence across life. Nonprofit and research-driven, built with Stanford and NVIDIA, it is one of the most significant genomics-specific AI efforts and is available openly.

players.name: NVIDIA BioNeMo
players.pls: BioNeMo is NVIDIA's platform for building and running AI models in drug discovery and life sciences, offering optimized biology foundation models, training tools, and an agent toolkit for scientific workflows. It packages models like Evo 2 and structure predictors for pharma and biotech teams, sitting underneath much of the field's compute.

players.name: Claude Science
players.pls: Anthropic's science workbench, launched in beta June 2026, wraps Claude with 60+ skills and connectors for genomics, proteomics, single-cell, and cheminformatics. It runs on a lab's own machines or HPC, orchestrates specialist models like Evo 2 and Boltz-2 via NVIDIA BioNeMo, and ships every figure with the code, environment, and history that produced it — reproducible by design.

players.name: Benchling
players.pls: Benchling is the cloud platform many life-science labs run on day to day — an electronic lab notebook, sample and inventory tracking, and R&D data management — increasingly layered with AI for analysis and search. Less a discovery model than the system of record where discovery happens, it is high-relevance infrastructure for working biologists.

players.name: Profluent
players.pls: Profluent uses protein language models to design novel proteins and gene-editing systems, and has reported the first AI-designed CRISPR editor built from scratch. Venture-backed with pharma partnerships, it applies generative AI to programmable biology, from editors to therapeutic proteins.

categories.name: Model Harnesses
categories.pls: A harness is the runtime scaffold wrapped around a model — the agentic loop that calls the model, runs tools, manages memory and context, and keeps going until the job is done. Unlike IDE-bound coding agents or the SDKs you build with, these are ready-to-run, model-agnostic (bring-your-own-key) programs you host yourself. The flagship coding agents Claude Code and OpenAI Codex are themselves harnesses, but this map keeps them under Coding Agents by their primary identity; the tools here lead with the harness itself.

players.name: OpenClaw
players.pls: The breakout open-source harness of 2026: run an autonomous agent you talk to from WhatsApp, Telegram, and 25+ channels, voice included. It shipped as Warelay, was renamed Clawdbot and then Moltbot (after an Anthropic trademark complaint) before settling on OpenClaw, and blew past 375,000 GitHub stars. Creator Steinberger joined OpenAI in February 2026 and a non-profit foundation now stewards it; under the hood it embeds Pi's SDK.

players.name: Hermes Agent
players.tagline: The open-source harness that grows with you
players.pls: Nous Research's open-source, model-agnostic harness — distinct from its Hermes LLM line that shares the name — turns any model into a long-running personal assistant. One gateway exposes the agent across Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, and CLI at once, with persistent memory, lineage-based context compression, and skills it writes for itself from successful runs. The v0.9.0 'everywhere release' (April 2026) drove fast adoption; it bets on agents that compound knowledge over time.

players.name: Goose
players.pls: Block's open-source agent went vendor-neutral in April 2026 when it was donated to the Linux Foundation's new Agentic AI Foundation. Goose runs in your terminal or as a desktop app, executes multi-step engineering tasks with any model provider behind it, and extends through MCP — a foundation-governed alternative to lab-owned CLIs.

players.name: OpenHands
players.tagline: Open-source platform for self-hosted coding agents
players.pls: Formerly OpenDevin, OpenHands is the MIT-licensed, open-source platform for running autonomous software-engineering agents — writing code, running tests, and opening pull requests inside sandboxed Docker environments. Bring-your-own-key and model-agnostic, it self-hosts with no vendor lock-in and scales from one local agent to fleets across an org. Past 80,000 GitHub stars and adopted by enterprises, it is the leading open alternative to closed agents like Devin.

players.name: Pi
players.pls: A minimal, reshapeable coding-agent harness from Mario Zechner, now at Earendil: four core tools (read, write, edit, bash), a TUI, and a unified LLM API spanning 15+ providers so the same agent loop runs on Claude, GPT, Gemini, or local models with your own keys. Lazy-loading skills keep prompts lean; TypeScript extensions rebuild the harness around your workflow.

players.name: SWE-agent
players.tagline: Princeton's research harness for GitHub issues
players.pls: The academic harness from the Princeton and Stanford team behind SWE-bench: SWE-agent takes a GitHub issue and fixes it with the language model of your choice, and is a standard research baseline (it also tackles cybersecurity and competitive-coding tasks). Its 100-line spin-off, mini-swe-agent — bash as the only tool — scores above 74% on SWE-bench Verified and is used by Meta, NVIDIA, and IBM as a benchmarking harness.
